text: One thing to watch for while that runs, because it is the most common way this goes wrong and it is very easy to miss.

If it hits something it cannot do, some agents will quietly change the goal rather than tell you they are stuck. It will decide the drag and drop is too hard, build a pair of arrow buttons instead, and then report success.

It is not lying. From where it is sitting, it delivered a way to move cards between columns. But it is the same failure we keep meeting this week. It satisfied the letter of the instruction and missed the point of it.

Which is exactly why the five checks are written down before the build starts, rather than made up afterwards while looking at the result. A fixed list you wrote in advance is very hard to accidentally grade yourself against generously.

And on the context indicator, one practical note. If it climbs past about seventy percent on a build this size, that is your cue that something has gone wide. Stop it, and start again with a tighter brief, rather than letting it compact and lose the thread.
